Class HolidayRuleSet

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.calendar.rule.HolidayRuleSet
public class HolidayRuleSet extends Object
The complete set of holiday rules from which the closures of a stock exchange are calculated.

Parsed from the YAML of a trading_calendar_rule_set row by HolidayRuleSetYamlParser. An exchange whose calendar is identical to another one -- the German regional venues follow Xetra, the Swiss venues follow SIX -- does not repeat the rules; its row points at the other row and HolidayRuleSetResolver merges the two. The identity of the set, its MIC and name, are columns of the entity and therefore not fields here.

    • closuresWithRuleName

      public SortedMap<LocalDate, String> closuresWithRuleName(int year)
      Returns the closures of the given year together with the name of the rule that produced each one. The comparison report uses the names to explain why a date was expected to be a closure.

      When two rules resolve to the same date -- which happens for instance when a fixed national day coincides with an Easter-relative holiday -- both names are kept, separated by a slash, so the overlap stays visible instead of one rule silently masking the other.

      Parameters:
      year - the year for which the closures are wanted
      Returns:
      map from closure date to rule name, in ascending date order, never null

    • halfDaysWithRuleName

      public SortedMap<LocalDate, String> halfDaysWithRuleName(int year)
      Returns the days in the given year on which the exchange only shortens its trading hours. These are not closures and are never part of closureDatesForYear(int), but the comparison report uses them to explain a disagreement: a shortened day sometimes yields no price data and is then wrongly recorded as a closure.
      Parameters:
      year - the year for which the half days are wanted
      Returns:
      map from date to rule name, in ascending date order, never null

    • validate

      public void validate()
      Validates every rule of this set. Whether a set without rules is acceptable is decided by the caller, because an empty set is valid exactly when the row extends another one, which is not visible here.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when the set or one of its rules is malformed
